title: Check every world claim
statement: Check every claim a text presents as true about the world at the precision its grade needs.
example: One ledger lists 32 claims across four short informational stories for an independent check.
detail: A factuality ledger written while four informational stories were being drafted lists every claim they present as true about the world, to be checked at Grade 3 precision (short causal statements, qualitative magnitudes) rather than journal precision, and sets a fiction boundary around invented particulars (`grade3-reading/artifacts/demo-unit-2026-07-10/02-factuality-claims.md`). Invented numbers carry no claim except where they embed a real rate or magnitude, which then gets its own row; a misconception a character voices is planted to be refuted, so the check is that the refutation is clear, and a character's absolute ("never") is that character's stance, not a taught universal. The ledger also checks that a text's claim about one river's delta does not become "every river builds a delta", and a film script's notes forbid claiming that all of London had no cars or electricity (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/video-2026-09-16/PETER-PAN-PART-1-FILM.md`). Nothing may be overgeneralized, invented details count as fiction unless they carry a real rate, and every misconception a character voices must be clearly corrected.
against: The ledger is a handoff written during drafting; it records the drafting loop's own verdicts, and the binding ones belong to a separate check it does not record (the same file, lines 3-6 and 11-13).
